text: [tactic-guide] mathlib 66k proofs: the dominant tactics by frequency are rw (46.9k uses), simp (29k), have (28.6k), exact (27.5k), refine (18k), obtain (12.6k), apply (11.5k), simpa (7.8k), intro (7.2k), ext (7.1k), simp_rw (5.5k), rcases (5.5k), by_cases (3.6k), induction (3k). A typical proof opens with intro/obtain, rewrites with rw, closes with exact or simp.

[tactic-guide] rw vs simp: rw rewrites with an equation left-to-right, needs the term to match syntactically; simp normalizes with the simp set and closes goals by itself. When simp makes no progress, try simp only [...], or find the right lemma with rw. simpa = simp + assumption, good for closing after normalization.

[tactic-guide] have vs obtain: have introduces an intermediate fact you prove inline (have h : P := ...); obtain (rcases) destructs an existential/conjunction from an existing hypothesis (obtain ⟨x, hx⟩ := h). Structured proofs chain obtain steps then refine/exact a named term.
[tactic-guide] ext tactic: applies an extensionality lemma automatically — for functions, sets, subgroups, filters. If the goal is f = g for functions, start with ext x.

[tactic-guide] NumberTheory style: proofs lean on rw (2.9k) + exact (1.3k) with modular-arithmetic lemmas (Int.ModEq, ZMod); congruences are rewritten as ModEq, not as equalities of sums. Analysis style: rw + have + simp with norm_num for concrete constants and field_simp for fractions.

[tactic-guide] omega closes goals over Nat/Int linear arithmetic including divisibility and mod; it is the default for concrete numeric goals. norm_num evaluates numeric expressions involving rationals, reals, powers, and constants like π. Both close goals fully — prefer them over manual rw chains.

[failure-mode] Restatement trap (seen in selflearner round 3): proposing an already-formalized theorem verbatim. Lean accepts it (it type-checks) but it duplicates mathlib. Before proposing, search the library for the concept's canonical name (e.g. slope_anti_adjacent) — if a statement of that shape exists, propose a genuinely different lemma or stop.

[failure-mode] Namespace trap (seen in rounds 4/5/7/8): citing a lemma as And.slope_anti_adjacent or a bare strictConcaveOn_sqrt_Ici fails when the name lives under a different namespace (StrictConcaveOn.slope_anti_adjacent lives in Mathlib.Analysis.Convex.Slope). Always check the exact fully-qualified name and add the file's import to the candidate.

[failure-mode] Triviality trap (seen in round 2 of the upgraded loop): theorem fixed : True := trivial type-checks and is novel-named, but carries zero information. A proposal must connect to the seed context's mathematical content — restate the goal in your own words before writing Lean; if the statement is True/False or provable by rfl alone, it is not worth admitting.

[failure-mode] Syntax slips seen at effort=minimal: unbalanced anonymous constructors ⟨⟩, expected token errors from malformed binders, applying iteratedFDeriv as if it were a function without its arguments, set_option traces quoted as commands. At effort=low with error feedback, 2/3 proposals compiled; at minimal without feedback, 1/13.

[selflearner-experience] Verified-write-only (M7.7 lesson): unverified derivations poison downstream composition — in a self-improving loop, every admitted fact must pass a machine checker first. Admission funnel: propose -> compile (Lean) -> novelty gate (no name collision, no one-line exact restatement) -> non-triviality gate (no True/False), then admit with provenance.

[selflearner-experience] The 2026-10-05 growth experiment: 16 proposal rounds at minimal effort yielded 1 compilable (7.7%), which was a restatement and was retracted. Upgrading proposer to effort=low with compile-error feedback retries yielded 2/3 compilable. Net genuine growth after all gates: IsCyclic.pow_eq_one_iff — finite cyclic group, t^a = 1 for all t iff a = 0 in ZMod d.
